note.text: Cameroon lies in central-western Africa, north of the Equator and east of Greenwich, with a coast on the Gulf of Guinea. Its neighbours are Nigeria, Chad, the Central African Republic, the Republic of the Congo, Gabon and Equatorial Guinea. Yaoundé is the capital; Douala is a major coastal city. The country extends from a humid coast towards the Lake Chad basin. Its surface area is about 475000 km²; published exact totals vary by source and convention, so this is deliberately approximate.

sections.heading: Your goal and connections
sections.text: By the end, you should be able to describe Cameroon’s position and neighbours and read a coordinate on a regional graticule. Builds on: Form Three’s coordinates and this term’s global biome comparisons. Leads to: Cameroon’s relief, rivers and climatic regions.

sections.heading: Explain the geography
sections.text: Cameroon lies in central-western Africa, north of the Equator and east of Greenwich, with a coast on the Gulf of Guinea. Its neighbours are Nigeria, Chad, the Central African Republic, the Republic of the Congo, Gabon and Equatorial Guinea. Yaoundé is the capital; Douala is a major coastal city. The country extends from a humid coast towards the Lake Chad basin. Its surface area is about {475000} km²; published exact totals vary by source and convention, so this is deliberately approximate.

sections.heading: Follow the local example or model
sections.text: Latitude describes north-south position; longitude describes east-west position. Cameroon’s length and relief help explain environmental contrasts, but latitude alone does not determine rainfall or land use. The exercise uses a fictional station on a regional graticule, not the measured location of a named town. A coordinate point does not represent the outline, area or administrative boundary of the whole country.

sections.heading: Apply and check
sections.text: Read hemisphere labels and write latitude before longitude. Distinguish a neighbouring country from an internal region and the Republic of the Congo from the Democratic Republic of the Congo. Use an atlas for precise boundaries and measurements. Do not treat an approximate area as an exact cadastral figure.

cards.idea: Distinguish the features before applying them.
example: absolute location: position described using geographical coordinates.
relative location: position described in relation to other places or features.
neighbouring states: countries sharing Cameroon’s land boundaries.
approximate area: a rounded measure of the country’s surface extent.

questions.prompt: Read classroom station P on this regional graticule. Choose latitude first, then longitude. P is fictional, not a surveyed town.

misconceptions.explain: That exchanges the latitude and longitude values.
The map labels north, not south, of the Equator.
The map labels east, not west, of Greenwich.

solution: Read the parallel through P and then its meridian.
